sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And what is the long-term impact to the Malay language, culture and tradition when a cultural motif is reduced to an AI output?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must be clear-sighted about what AI can and cannot offer and always ask what is the purpose AI is serving and whether it is fit for that purpose?

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must avoid being boxed in into an AI-centric gaze in which we are left with a narrow and artificially mediated understanding of reality and an impoverished capacity to make sense of and relate to the world and those around us.

sections.label: Sitting suspended
sections.summary: The Sitting is suspended at 3.51 pm and the Chair will be taken at 4.10 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Order, we have been in the Chambers for close to five hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.10 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.51 pm until 4.10 pm.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Premium AI Access Scheme
sections.summary: The Government partially adopted Gerald Giam's 2024 suggestions, with the SkillsFuture Premium AI Access Scheme giving six months of free tools to Singaporeans in selected courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government has partially adopted the 2024 suggestions of my colleague Gerald Giam to provide universal premium AI model access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Premium AI Access Scheme, six months of free tools for Singaporeans who enrol in selected courses, is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These are good starts, but they are unnecessarily gated behind course enrolment and union membership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And critically, they likely will not cover AI agents – the tier where the real productivity gap will open.

sections.label: Universal premium AI access question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will make premium AI access a universal entitlement rather than gating it behind course completion or union membership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Government make premium AI access a universal entitlement, rather than gate it behind course completion or union membership?

sections.label: Frontier AI firms as strategic
sections.summary: The passage says frontier AI firms should be treated with the same strategic seriousness as bilateral relations with countries, and Singapore should seek bulk licensing agreements for agent-tier access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When Anthropic or OpenAI decides what to charge for agent-tier access or whom to serve, that decision shapes Singapore's productivity frontier as directly as any trade agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should therefore treat this class of companies – frontier AI firms that have crossed a threshold of systemic importance – with the same strategic seriousness that we bring to bilateral relations with countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the possible future where frontier AI agent costs go up, not down, Singapore should seek bulk licensing agreements for agent-tier access the same way we negotiate energy supply.

sections.label: Water reuse and data centres
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore is among world leaders in water reuse and integrated water management, a binding constraint on data centre expansion in water-scarce Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We would be competing with some of the highest cost bases in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And we are among the world's leaders in water reuse and integrated water management, which is a binding constraint on data centre expansion across water-scarce regions in Southeast Asia.

sections.label: Retrenchment and PMET incidence figures
sections.summary: MOM's Q4 2025 report recorded about 14,490 retrenchments in 2025, up from about 13,000, with PMET incidence at 10.1 per 1,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOM's own fourth quarter of 2025 Labour Market Report reported about 14,490 retrenchments in 2025, up from about 13,000 the year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: PMET retrenchment incidence reached 10.1 per 1,000 resident employees, above the pre-recessionary norm of 8.0 set during 2015 to 2019.

sections.label: AI restructuring worker protections
sections.summary: It proposes a 90-day transition notice, redeployment-first obligation, and workers' ability to challenge termination reasons for AI restructuring protections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, a 90-day mandatory transition notice before AI-driven role elimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, a re-deployment-first obligation, retraining or reassignment before AI-driven termination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, for workers to be able to substantively challenge the reasons for their termination if they feel they are misleading, so that these AI restructuring protections will be real.

sections.label: Preference for employment over UBI
sections.summary: When offered a choice between universal basic income and employment, people invariably choose employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: People, when offered the choice between a universal basic income and employment, invariably choose employment.

sections.label: Strategic engagement and retrenchment framework
sections.summary: It calls for strategic engagement and a retrenchment framework where the automating company bears the cost before the worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Strategic engagement, so we are not price-takers in our own future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And a retrenchment framework where the company that decides to automate bears the cost of that decision before the worker does.

sections.label: DBS reducing contract and temporary staff
sections.summary: DBS Bank announced plans to reduce contract and temporary staff by around 4,000 across various markets with AI adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Closer to home, DBS Bank has announced plans to reduce its contract and temporary staff by around 4,000 across various markets, with AI adoption.

sections.label: Chinese courts on AI dismissals
sections.summary: Chinese courts reviewed AI-related dismissal cases, with one arbitration panel finding AI replacement not valid grounds for dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As mentioned by some Members, recently, courts in China have been active in reviewing cases regarding the dismissal of employees due to AI-related restructuring and choosing to protect labour rights against unfair AI-related lay-offs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In one case, the arbitration panel clarified that AI replacement was not valid grounds for dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In another case, a massive role and salary reduction due to AI taking over the work was not considered a reasonable re-assignment proposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, companies must be held to a human transition standard.

sections.label: PMET retrenchment and unemployment
sections.summary: Prolonged unemployment and income loss affect loved ones, with MOM data showing rising PMET retrenchments versus 2019 pre-recession norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It can mean prolonged unemployment, income loss and long-term repercussions for their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And this we are already seeing in the data that is provided by MOM, where there has been a rise in PMET retrenchments compared to the pre-recession norms in 2019, reflecting their greater exposure to sectors undergoing restructuring.

sections.label: SBS Transit AI bus maintenance
sections.summary: SBS Transit overhauled bus maintenance with AI diagnostics, creating a diagnostic expert career scheme for over 50 workers instead of cutting jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SBS Transit, with support from the National Transport Workers Union and the CTC Grant, overhauled its bus maintenance operations using AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The company implemented AI-powered diagnostic systems for predictive maintenance and instead of cutting jobs, it created a new diagnostic expert career scheme for over 50 workers.

sections.label: NTUC AI skills partnerships
sections.summary: NTUC partners AWS and Huawei to equip 100,000 workers and 100 enterprises with AI skills, with union support for AI subscription fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More recently, NTUC is partnering global technology leaders, like Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Huawei, to equip 100,000 workers and 100 enterprises with AI skills through the CTC ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the individual level, union members can also tap on union support for up to half of the subscription fees for AI models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is in addition to the six-month subscription provided through the Government.

sections.label: Technology alone does not determine success
sections.summary: Factories with the best technology struggle due to misalignment and distrust when workers, unions, management and government do not move together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It is not the machine, nor the technology that determines success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I have seen factories with the best technology money can buy struggle because of misalignment, because of distrust, because workers, unions, management and government were not moving in the same direction.

sections.label: Tripartite partnership protecting workers
sections.summary: The tripartite partnership between NTUC, Singapore National Employees Federation and the Government works well, as unions protect workers, not just jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: From my enterprise experience, our tripartite partnership between the NTUC, Singapore National Employees Federation and the Government is unique, so unique that many of my overseas colleagues are genuinely puzzled by how well it works with real positive outcomes for all, because our unions do not just protect jobs, they protect workers.

sections.label: Government support for AI access
sections.summary: Government provides support structures, skills frameworks and training pathways, with NTUC subsidising AI subscriptions so AI stays accessible to the masses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: And the Government must provide the support structure, strong skills framework, accessible training pathways and broad-based access to technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: That is why I am encouraged by the support the Government is providing to help Singaporeans adopt AI tools, further strengthened by NTUC's initiative to subsidise AI subscription to its members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is important because AI cannot become a tool only for the privileged few.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It must remain accessible to the masses so that every worker has the opportunity to improve productivity, strengthen capabilities and participate meaningfully in Singapore's next phase of growth.

sections.label: Enterprise transformation and job redesign
sections.summary: In a tight labour market, enterprise and industry transformation must go hand in hand with business process re-engineering and job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In a tight labour market, like Singapore, this enterprise and industry transformation must go hand in hand with deep business process re-engineering and meaningful job redesign, as mentioned by a few of the Members here.

sections.label: Tax incentives and worker support schemes
sections.summary: Tax incentives help companies invest in AI tools, while schemes support workers through job redesign, training and wage support during upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The tax incentives help companies invest in the necessary AI tools and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But equally important are the schemes that support workers through this transition, whether it is programmes such as the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant, NTUC CTC Grant, the Union Training Assistance Programme, and Workforce Singapore's Career Conversion Programmes, these initiatives support job redesign, training and even provide wage support while workers undergo upskilling and reskilling.

sections.label: Opportunity cannot be left to market
sections.summary: If left unaddressed, these issues can divide society, so opportunity for all cannot be left to market forces alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: If left unaddressed, they can divide our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: That is why this opportunity for all cannot be left to market forces alone, a point also raised by Member Poh Li San.

sections.label: Risk of jobless growth
sections.summary: Growth will bring new roles, but if workers' skills are not ready, there is a risk of jobless growth from a jobs-skills mismatch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Because growth will come and new roles will emerge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But if our workers are not ready, if skills are not kept in pace, we risk a different kind of jobless growth – not a lack of jobs, but a mismatch between jobs and the skills our workforce has.

sections.label: Continuous upgrading and community support
sections.summary: Workers must continuously reskill and upskill using support from Workforce Singapore, NTUC, and community initiatives such as M3+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: That is why we must be prepared to continuously upgrade ourselves – to reskill and upskill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is where it is important for us to make use of the support available – whether through Workforce Singapore (WSG) programmes, NTUC, or community initiatives, such as M3+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: At M3+ Pasir Ris–Changi, for example, we run various programmes to help the community enhance their skills and employment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: These include Women-at-Work to help women return to the workforce, as well as the Career Marketplace held in Pasir Ris to open access to career opportunities and employment networks.

sections.label: AI for Malay language and culture
sections.summary: AI can digitalise Jawi manuscripts, produce batik designs, facilitate Malay language learning and translation, and preserve classic Malay films.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: AI can assist in digitalising old Jawi manuscripts, producing batik designs inspired by traditional Malay motifs and facilitating the learning and translation of the Malay language.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Even classic Malay films can be preserved for future generations.

sections.label: Renewing the social compact
sections.summary: The transformation is a test of the social compact, which must be renewed so workers, businesses and Government move forward together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, at its heart, this is not just an economic transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This is a test of our social compact, a compact that must now be renewed for a new era where businesses commit to not just profits but to people, where workers commit to not just jobs, but to lifelong growth, and where the Government continues to stand with both, ensuring that no one is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: If we can do this, if we can move forward together with trust, purpose and shared responsibility, this transformation will not divide us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It will make us stronger because when workers, businesses and the Government move together, we do not just adapt to change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We shape it, we benefit from it and we ensure that every Singaporean moves forward together.

sections.label: Jobless growth not an option
sections.summary: Jobless growth is not an option for Singapore because good jobs are integral to inclusive growth and a fair society.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, jobless growth is not an option for Singapore as good jobs are integral to inclusive growth and to a fair and vibrant society.

sections.label: Structural social support schemes
sections.summary: Workfare Income Supplement and Silver Support provide structural support, and SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support gives income relief to the involuntarily unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is more structural or permanent social support in the form of the Workfare Income Supplement and Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And the Government, recognising the greater risk of economic and job disruption, has introduced income relief for the involuntarily unemployed through SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support, which has been discussed by Members of this House.

sections.label: Employment rates of young graduates
sections.summary: The response received, reaffirmed yesterday, was that employment rates for young degree holders have remained broadly stable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The response I received then, which was reaffirmed yesterday as well, was that employment rates for young degree holders has remained broadly stable.

sections.label: AI adoption impact on jobs
sections.summary: As AI adoption grows, benefits to productivity and profits rise but so does the impact on jobs, requiring support and equipping citizens.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the pace of AI adoption picks up, however, the benefits to firm productivity and profits will grow, but so too will the impact on jobs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While we must consider the need for greater social support and new channels of redistribution to keep our society inclusive, we must also continue to equip citizens to provide for themselves through good jobs and incomes.

sections.label: Singapore Opportunity Index by MOM
sections.summary: The Singapore Opportunity Index developed by MOM highlights how employers can create opportunities through recruitment, career pathways and job design.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Opportunity Index developed by MOM highlights how employers can create opportunities for their workers such as through recruitment practices, career development pathways and job design.

sections.label: Graduate share of resident workforce
sections.summary: Over 40% of the resident workforce today hold university degrees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, over 40% of the resident workforce have university degrees.

sections.label: Singapore as job redesign reference
sections.summary: Singapore should build expertise as a global reference point for skills-first and human-centric job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My fourth point is that Singapore should build up expertise as a global reference point for skills-first and human-centric job redesign.

sections.label: Institute for Adult Learning papers
sections.summary: The Institute for Adult Learning's Centre for Skills-First Practices launched skills-first working papers and roundtable discussions that drew international participation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Institute for Adult Learning’s Centre for Skills-First Practices recently launched a series of skills-first working papers and accompanying roundtable discussions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They attracted much international attention, with participation from experts, policy-makers and industry practitioners around the world.

sections.label: Adult learning centres and institutes
sections.summary: Polytechnics, ITE, SMU, SIT and SUSS host workplace learning, workforce and skills initiatives, and the Institute for Adult Learning can be a national focal point.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, the polytechnics and ITE are among the national centres of excellence for workplace learning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Singapore Management University has set up a Resilient Workforces Institute, while the Singapore Institute of Technology has launched a Skills Assessment and Validation initiative.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the Singapore University of Social Sciences, the Institute for Adult Learning has an Adult Learning Collaboratory and a Centre for Skills-First Practices.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With end-to-end expertise from research to translation, the Institute for Adult Learning can serve as a national focal point for adult learning and employability.

sections.label: National AI and Tripartite Jobs Councils
sections.summary: The National AI Council and the Tripartite Jobs Council were formed, underscoring this commitment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The formation of the National AI Council and the Tripartite Jobs Council underscores this commitment.

sections.label: PME upskilling and automation fears
sections.summary: An NTUC survey found over half of PMEs feel an urgent need to upskill, and other studies show half of Singaporeans fear role automation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: A recent NTUC survey found that more than half of our PMEs feel an urgent need to upskill just to stay relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Nearly a third are actively anxious about being replaced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Other studies have shown that half of Singaporeans fear that their roles could be automated, and many are concerned that AI will benefit the bottom-lines of corporations more than it benefits the everyday worker.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and AI adoption
sections.summary: Singapore's lifelong learning investments through SkillsFuture position it well for AI adoption, including a programme targeting 10,000 enterprises and 100,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: For years, we have proactively anticipated a disruption like this, by investing and imbuing in Singaporeans the value of lifelong learning and the need to regularly upskill through programmes, such as SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This has put us in a good starting position as we push hard on AI adoption, like the National AI Impact Programme that aims to support 10,000 enterprises and help 100,000 workers become more AI fluent.

sections.label: National AI literacy and fluency
sections.summary: The passage calls for a national AI literacy programme and for workers to be given time and ability to apply AI tools at work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: If embracing AI is a national strategic move, then we should roll out a national AI literacy and fluency programme for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Second, supporting workers to become AI fluent should be more than just providing them with the AI tools and the know-how on using them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We must also equip and afford workers the time and ability to learn how to apply the AI tools in their workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Getting young graduates past the door, and securing older workers and PMEs in new roles are imperative, but if AI is to transform our economy, we must ensure that our workforce learns effectively through deeper learning while persuading our businesses and organisations to create workplaces and systems that allow our workers to test their new skills, learn from mistakes and improve.

sections.label: Market intelligence and foresight system
sections.summary: The speaker supports a Singapore-contextualised market intelligence and foresight system, and suggests using it to incentivise AI startups to create jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Before I conclude, I wish to support the proposal by NTUC Secretary-General, Mr Ng Chee Meng, for the setting up of a market intelligence and foresight system contextualised to the Singapore market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We can appreciate how useful it would be to draw insights from information, data points, analysis and the research of tripartite partners to sense-make for early signals, coordinate responses and provide proactive early intervention, where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: That said, while supporting our workers to retrain and move on to different roles to prevent displacement is important, we should also explore the possibility of using information from the same system to identify how the Government can incentivise AI startups to create new jobs and opportunities for our workforce.

sections.label: EDB expected jobs created
sections.summary: EDB announced expected jobs created fell to 15,700 this year, the lowest in at least 20 years, despite attracting more investments than the year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Economic Development Board (EDB) announced that the expected number of jobs to be created fell to 15,700, the lowest in at least 20 years, despite having attracted more investments than the year before.

sections.label: Fair and responsible retrenchment standards
sections.summary: The passage calls for raising standards for fair retrenchment, including early notifications, union negotiation of benefits and AI grant conditions on redeployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As a start, we need to raise our standards for what constitutes fair and responsible retrenchment, such as by requiring early retrenchment notifications, supporting unions to negotiate for retrenchment benefits according to industry norms and designing AI grant incentives with conditions requiring employers to demonstrate efforts to meaningfully re-deploy workers whose roles and tasks are taken over by AI.

sections.label: Jobseeker Support income threshold
sections.summary: The Jobseeker Support Scheme's $5,000 income threshold covers under 20% of resident PMEs, and the speaker hopes it is raised to $8,400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The income threshold for Jobseeker Support Scheme is currently set at $5,000 excluding CPF, which would only cover less than 20% of resident PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will consider raising this threshold to the gross median resident PME income, currently at $8,400 as of 2025, or consider some other suitable schemes of equivalence to address the needs of impacted PMEs.

sections.label: AI guesses personal characteristics
sections.summary: A joint SUTD-GovTech study found large learning models can reliably guess personal characteristics from other data points even when resumes are anonymised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: A joint Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)-GovTech study found that large learning models can reliably guess personal characteristics, like gender of candidate from other data points like hobbies and volunteering, even when resumes are anonymised.

sections.label: AI workplace use recommendations
sections.summary: Employers adopting employment-related AI should conduct risk assessments, ensure human oversight, support HR training, and work with vendors on fairness and transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, that employers who adopt employment-related AI be guided to conduct risk assessments proportionate to the level of impact and ensure meaningful human oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, that HR professionals be supported with training and self-assessment tools to use AI responsibly and identify biasness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: They should know where AI is being used in decisions that affect them, what guardrails are in place and how existing avenues of redress apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And fourth, that we explore going upstream, working with AI vendors and developers to ensure that the underlying software meets some baseline principles of fairness and transparency before it reaches our workplaces.

sections.label: TTSH Smart Scheduler rostering
sections.summary: At Tan Tock Seng Hospital, HSEU and management rolled out a Smart Scheduler that cut rostering time from over 90 minutes to under 15.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH), where our Healthcare Services Employees' Union (HSEU) worked with management through the CTC to roll out a Smart Scheduler that could handle multiple shift patterns and cut rostering time from more than 90 minutes to under 15, so that nurse managers could spend more time on other core work instead.

sections.label: Broadening Jobseeker Support eligibility
sections.summary: The eligibility criteria for Jobseeker Support assistance can be broadened so more PMEs benefit and have greater security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The eligibility criteria for Jobseeker Support assistance can be broadened, so that more PMEs can benefit and have greater security.

sections.label: Fair deal for workers
sections.summary: Where companies benefit from operating and growing in Singapore, a fair deal for workers will be expected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Where companies benefit from operating and growing in Singapore, we will expect a fair deal for workers.

sections.label: Exposure of repetitive roles
sections.summary: Roles built primarily around repeating the same steps are the most exposed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Roles built primarily around repeating the same steps are the most exposed.

sections.label: Support for PMEs and displaced workers
sections.summary: The committee recognises PMEs face greater job uncertainty and will recommend targeted support, including Jobseeker Support enhancements and placement help.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: On PMEs specifically, the committee recognises that they may face greater job uncertainties and will recommend more targeted support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: This includes considering enhancements to the Jobseeker Support Scheme, as Mr Patrick Tay suggested, and tapping on private sector expertise to strengthen placement support for this group.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: For workers at risk of displacement, the Economic Strategy Review will recommend practical ways to help them move into more resilient roles with stronger demand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We will identify sectors with sustained labour demand and lower AI displacement risk, and we will work with unions and employers in those sectors to create clear, supported entry points for workers making the transition.

sections.label: Raising floor, widening door
sections.summary: The response is to raise the floor and widen the door.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Our response is to raise the floor and widen the door.

sections.label: AI courses and tools access
sections.summary: From second half of 2026, IHLs offer alumni discounted AI courses for a year, and Singaporeans completing selected AI courses get six months premium AI tools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: From the second half of 2026, all of our IHLs will offer selected AI-related courses at significant discounts for their alumni, for a period of one year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: For workers already in the workforce, Singaporeans who complete selected AI training courses will receive six months of complimentary access to premium AI tools.

sections.label: Worker outcomes for public resources
sections.summary: Where public resources are deployed, worker outcomes will be asked for.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Where public resources are deployed, we will ask for worker outcomes.

sections.label: Company reskilled and redeployed workers
sections.summary: The company reskilled and redeployed more than 2,000 workers into higher-skilled roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: At the same time, the company reskilled and redeployed more than 2,000 workers into higher-skilled roles.

sections.label: Maxi-Cash reskilled sales advisors
sections.summary: Maxi-Cash reskilled 25 sales advisors to use an AI-enabled authentication system that assesses jewellery composition in five seconds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Maxi-Cash enhanced this process by reskilling 25 of their sales advisors to use an AI-enabled authentication system, which can accurately assess the composition of jewellery in just five seconds.

sections.label: Sharing AI benefits widely
sections.summary: If Singapore succeeds in its AI ambitions, the Government will ensure the benefits are widely shared among all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: If Singapore succeeds with our AI ambitions – and we should never assume success is automatic, because it will require sustained effort, difficult choices, adaptation and perhaps, some good fortune too.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: But if we succeed, then the Government will ensure that the benefits are widely shared.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: The gains must not accrue only to those who already have capital, advantages or access.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: They must translate into better wages, better opportunities and greater security for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Reviewing education for AI age
sections.summary: The education system will be reviewed to develop qualities that give Singaporeans competitive advantage in an AI age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: In an AI age, they will become the hard edge of competitive advantage for our people and for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: That is why we will review our education system, to make sure we develop these qualities with the same rigour and intentionality we have always applied to academic excellence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Our human brains are muscles that require exercise, and genuine mastery – the kind that holds up under pressure and that AI cannot simply replace – comes from hard work, from practice and from deep understanding.

sections.label: Students asking unexpected questions
sections.summary: A student who asks unexpected questions and pursues deep interests may be ahead in the world being built.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: A student who asks the unexpected questions, who pursues something deeply out of genuine interest, who can hold two contradictory ideas and work through them – that student is not behind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: In the world that we are building, that student may be ahead of all of us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We are committed to doing this, together with our educators, our parents and young Singaporeans themselves.

sections.label: Supporting workers through disruption
sections.summary: No one should face disruption alone, and workers should move forward as the economy grows.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Some will face real disruption and our responsibility is to ensure no one faces it alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: And we will ensure that as our economy grows, our workers move forward with it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: If we develop Singaporeans who are curious, creative and deeply human, people who can ask the questions that machines cannot and earn the trust that algorithms never will, then we will not merely manage this transition.

sections.label: Seniors' AI access and training
sections.summary: The issue is lack of access and confidence, not willingness, with residents aged 50 to 64 having the lowest training participation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: This encouraged me because it shows that the issue is not a lack of willingness, but rather a lack of access and, to some extent, to some of them, it is about confidence, which we can overcome by curating and customising access to AI tools and making time for our seniors to learn and to increase their knowledge.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We see a gap in training participation, where MOM's 2025 report found that residents aged 50 to 64 had the lowest training participation rate at 44.5%, compared with about 60% for those who are below 40 years old.

sections.label: Older adults' learning gaps
sections.summary: OECD and Pew reports show learning-by-doing opportunities and AI use at work fall with age.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: OECD's Employment Outlook 2025 highlights that across OECD countries, opportunities to learn by doing fall with age, where 62% of adults aged 25 to 29 reported such opportunities, but this falls to 45% among those who are 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In addition, a 2025 Pew Research Centre report found that 73% of workers who used AI at work were aged 18 to 49, while only 27% were aged 50 and above.

sections.label: LearningHub AI course enrolment
sections.summary: Since February 2026, more than 4,000 workers have enrolled in LearningHub's AI courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Since February 2026, more than 4,000 workers have enrolled in LearningHub's AI courses.

sections.label: AI-Ready SG subscription subsidies
sections.summary: Under AI-Ready SG, union members get subsidies of up to 50% for AI premium subscription tools through UTAP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: At the same time, under AI-Ready SG, we are also closing the access gap by providing union members with subsidies of up to 50% for AI premium subscription tools through NTUC's Union Training Assistance Programme (UTAP).

sections.label: NTUC CTCs and transformation projects
sections.summary: NTUC has formed 3,800 CTCs and over 900 business transformation projects, benefiting over 300,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To date, NTUC has formed 3,800 CTCs, embarked on over 900 business transformation projects, benefiting over 300,000 workers.

sections.label: New system order processing results
sections.summary: The new system cut manual order processing by about 60%, letting the company handle 40% more orders and give wage increments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: With this new system, manual work such as order processing was reduced by about 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: As they became more productive, the company could handle 40% more orders and provide wage increments for its employees.

sections.label: Tripartite solidarity and AI opportunities
sections.summary: Tripartite partners moving in solidarity made firms more productive, gave workers better jobs and pay, and strengthened Singapore's competitiveness, building on Government, employer and Labour Movement efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Because tripartite partners moved together in solidarity, firms became more productive, workers took on better jobs with better pay and Singapore strengthened its competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: It will build on efforts across the Government, employers and the Labour Movement and enable partners to scale outreach, accelerate policy implementation and direct resources so that workers and enterprises can seize opportunities from AI.

sections.label: NTUC AI-Ready SG launch
sections.summary: In February this year, NTUC launched the AI-Ready SG initiative to encourage workers to learn and master AI tools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In February this year, the NTUC launched the AI-Ready SG initiative, actively encouraging workers to learn and master AI tools.

sections.label: Inclusive progress for every worker
sections.summary: The passage calls for upskilling and learning from younger colleagues to close access and skills gaps and expand opportunities for all workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Take that step with us, upskill and learn, including from your younger colleagues and together, we can close the access gap, narrow the skills gap and expand opportunities for all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Because in Singapore, we have always believed that progress must be inclusive, that as we move forward, we move forward together, because every worker matters.

sections.label: AI cuts and rehiring surveys
sections.summary: Global surveys show two in three companies that made AI-driven cuts are rehiring, and a MOM study shows about 6% of Singapore firms reduced headcount due to AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Recent global surveys show that two in three companies that made earlier AI-driven cuts are already rehiring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the preparation for my speech today, my team used AI to help refine the work to me.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It surfaced useful references, including our MOM's newly released study showing only about 6% of firms in Singapore have reduced headcount due to AI adoption.

sections.label: National AI strategies and investment
sections.summary: Singapore formed its first National AI Strategy in 2019, refreshed it in 2023, and planned to invest over $1 billion in AI compute, talent and industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our current efforts build on a strong foundation of work already done in this space.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We formed our first National AI Strategy in 2019, well before the introduction of ChatGPT and we embarked on national AI projects in areas such as education, healthcare, logistics, security and municipal services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: When large language models exploded onto the scene in late 2022, making AI accessible and general-purpose, we refreshed our strategies with the National AI Strategy 2.0 in 2023 and developed plans to invest over $1 billion in AI compute capabilities, talent and industry development.

sections.label: Proposed National AI Equity Fund
sections.summary: Mr Giam proposed a National AI Equity Fund to pay every Singapore Citizen $500, funded by companies that benefit from AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Mr Giam proposed a National AI Equity Fund to pay every Singapore Citizen $500 funded by the companies that benefit from AI.

sections.label: Surplus for upskilling, workforce spending
sections.summary: The passage says AI surplus is better used to fund upskilling, and the Government spent over $10 billion on local workforce initiatives in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The better use of any surplus generated by AI adoption is to fund accessible and effective upskilling that amplifies Singaporeans' value.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And to that end, the Government has spent over $10 billion over the last five years on local workforce initiatives.

sections.label: AI augmenting labour, firm survey
sections.summary: An inaugural survey shows AI is augmenting rather than replacing labour, with about 6% of adopting firms reporting reduced headcount and seven in 10 seeing productivity gains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our inaugural survey of the firms shows that AI is currently augmenting, rather than replacing labour in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Only about three in 10 firms have adopted AI currently, and amongst the firms that have adopted AI, only a small minority, about 6%, reported reduced headcount.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: More commonly, firms are redesigning jobs, they are creating new AI-related roles, indicating that AI is changing how work is done, how they are being re-organised, rather than reducing jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And seven in 10 firms using AI are already seeing productivity gains.

sections.label: Free AI tools for SkillsFuture courses
sections.summary: From the second half of this year, Singaporeans in selected SkillsFuture AI courses get six months of free premium AI tool access.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: From the second half of this year, Singaporeans who enrol in the selected SkillsFuture AI courses will receive six months of free access to premium AI tools.

sections.label: Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package funding
sections.summary: Over $400 million has been set aside for the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package to support businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Third, to support businesses, I have also emphasised time and again that we have set aside over $400 million for the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit for businesses
sections.summary: Later this year, eligible businesses will receive $10,000 under the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit to offset eligible workforce transformation programme costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Later this year, eligible businesses will also receive $10,000 under the redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit and this can be used to offset out-of-pocket costs for eligible workforce transformation programmes, including those under the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package.

sections.label: NTUC CTC Grant top-up and extension
sections.summary: The Government topped up the NTUC CTC Grant by around $200 million in 2025 and extended it to 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Government topped up the NTUC CTC Grant by around $200 million in 2025 and extended the grant to 2028.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme, launched last year, provides temporary financial relief and job search support to involuntarily unemployed individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have recognised for some time that we must strengthen our support mechanisms as the pace of change accelerates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is why we launched the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support scheme (JSS) last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The JSS provides temporary financial relief and job search support to involuntarily unemployed individuals.

sections.label: Proposal to raise JS income threshold
sections.summary: Mr Ng Chee Meng and Mr Patrick Tay proposed raising the JS scheme income threshold to better support higher-income individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Mr Ng Chee Meng and Mr Patrick Tay proposed to raise the JS scheme income threshold to better support higher-income individuals.

sections.label: Retrenchment notification duration review
sections.summary: Tripartite partners are discussing shortening retrenchment notification duration under the Employment Act review, with notification to Government by the last day of work where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Tripartite partners are already discussing shortening the retrenchment notification duration under the ongoing Employment Act review.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We, on our part, would like to see notification to the Government happening before or by the last day of work of the affected workers as far as possible, because then this would also enable a timelier employment facilitation support to workers.

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council approach
sections.summary: The Tripartite Jobs Council will take a coordinated tripartite approach to mobilise enterprises and workers towards fair and resilient growth in an AI era.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Jobs Council will take a coordinated tripartite approach to mobilise enterprises and workers towards fair and resilient growth in an AI era.

sections.label: Government help for business transformation
sections.summary: The Government will help businesses transform and compete, shaping an inclusive transformation so Singaporeans are co-pilots in the AI journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For all of our businesses, if you are unsure, you are uncertain as to where to start, you do not have to figure it out alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will help you to transform, will help you to compete so that together you can create better opportunities both for your businesses and for your workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will not leave the future of work, the livelihoods of our workers, our Singaporeans, to chance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will shape a transformation that is inclusive, forward thinking, anchored in real action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Singaporeans will never be helpless passengers to an AI-driven future, but Singaporeans will be our fellow co-pilots as our AI journey takes flight.

sections.label: Workers' share of AI gains
sections.summary: A question asks how the Government intends to ensure workers receive a direct and tangible share of AI productivity gains beyond more training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Can the Minister elaborate on how the Government intends to ensure workers receive a direct and tangible share of AI productivity gains beyond just more training?

sections.label: SWDA key performance index outcomes
sections.summary: SWDA will have clear key performance index outcomes tying the Enterprise Workforce Training Package and job redesign to real wage and career progression improvements for workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For today's Motion, the NTUC Secretary-General will be wrapping up.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But in the months, in the years ahead, I have shared that SWDA will have very clear key performance index outcomes, including tying the Enterprise Workforce Training Package, job redesign to specific skin in the game for both the businesses tapping on such grants, to improvement in real wages and career progression for the workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: That is how we envisage the pie to be shared.

sections.label: Tracking companies' job redesign
sections.summary: A speaker asks what mechanisms will track and recognise companies doing job redesign well, and says this should be discussed with tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: And I am very glad to hear that the Ministry has set out expectations of companies that benefit from AI and a vision for good jobs in the AI age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: I am also very happy to hear that you have committed by saying that public support will come with worker outcome expectations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: And what kind of mechanisms will you be putting in place to track and recognise companies that do this job redesign well?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: I think this is something that we should discuss together with all of our tripartite partners, whether it is with unions as well as business leaders, to make sure that any of our grant and support schemes do not end up making things even harder for companies that want to transform.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: But yes, this is the direction that we are committed towards and we should discuss this further in the coming months.

sections.label: 90-day notice definitional ambiguity
sections.summary: Speaker asks how companies, especially SMEs, determine when the 90-day notice formally commences, and whether rigid definitions may worsen worker outcomes and slow AI adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: The issue is therefore operational reality and definitional ambiguity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: So, could the Member clarify how companies, especially many of our SMEs, are expected to determine when this 90-day notice should formally commence?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Would the Member also agree that if definitions are too rigid, firms may avoid gradual redesign altogether and may instead move towards sharper restructuring exercises, which may ironically worsen outcomes for workers, and another possibility that this might even inadvertently cause slower AI adoption and weaken business competitiveness?

sections.label: Government shaping AI growth
sections.summary: Speaker says the Government has affirmed through the Motion that it will shape AI growth deliberately rather than leave outcomes to chance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As Minister Tan See Leng and Minister of State Ms Jasmin Lau have pointed out, left to the market, AI growth may not automatically benefit workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Members like Mr Yip Hon Weng warned about an outcome where some workers gain but others risk falling behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I am therefore glad that through this Motion, the Government has affirmed that it will not leave outcomes to chance, but will shape the direction of AI growth deliberately and I look forward to the measures that will be unveiled through the Economic Strategy Review report.

sections.label: Tripartite Jobs Council formation
sections.summary: Speaker says the Tripartite Jobs Council consolidates tripartite partners' capabilities, and welcomes Government support for NTUC's proposal to form it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: He also suggested that trade associations and chambers could become platforms that accelerate AI adoption across sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: This is exactly what the Tripartite Jobs Council is setting out to do – to consolidate tripartite partners' various capabilities under one roof to better serve out our enterprises and our workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I am glad the Government has supported NTUC's proposal to form this Tripartite Jobs Council.

sections.label: Public support and worker outcomes
sections.summary: Minister of State Ms Jasmin Lau shared the Government's commitment that where public support is given, companies are expected to support worker outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: In response, Minister of State Ms Jasmin Lau shared that the Government's commitment that where public support is given, the Government will expect companies to make the effort to support worker outcomes.

sections.label: Patrick Tay's 3 Es
sections.summary: Mr Patrick Tay called for the 3 Es and to raise Jobseeker Support eligibility to the PME median income of around $8,400 as of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: On the fourth move to enable displaced workers to bounce back with dignity and confidence, Mr Patrick Tay called on the "3 Es" – equitable growth, enhanced protections and engaged workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: He calls to raise the Jobseeker Support scheme eligibility to the PME median income – around $8,400 as of 2025 – and to provide earlier notification of retrenchment.

sections.label: Redundancy insurance scheme proposal
sections.summary: Mr Andre Low questioned whether the JSS is sufficient and proposed a redundancy insurance scheme instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Mr Andre Low questioned whether the JSS is sufficient and proposed a redundancy insurance scheme instead.

sections.label: Tripartite partners innovate together
sections.summary: Working closely with tripartite partners produced Workfare, the Progressive Wage Model and now the JSS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We will work closely with tripartite partners to innovate, as we have done before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: That is how we have come up with Workfare, Progressive Wage Model and now the JSS.

sections.label: Tripartite model based on trust
sections.summary: The tripartite model works because it is based on trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Our tripartite model works because it is based on trust.

sections.label: Tripartite model in AI era
sections.summary: Transformation in the AI era can be win-win, and the tripartite model in the AI era will ensure this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Transformation in the AI era can be win-win, and our tripartite model in the AI era will ensure this.

sections.label: Commitment to workers and enterprises
sections.summary: The House commits to keeping workers and enterprises at the heart of national efforts to seize AI opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We may not agree with every "how", but we must set the right direction, and at the same time, know with humility that we are innovating and experimenting with pathways forward in this era.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We have forged a firm commitment – to keep our workers and enterprises at the heart of national efforts to seize new opportunities brought about by AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: And in this Chamber, now it sends a clear signal to every worker – blue- and white-collared alike – this House stands with you.

sections.label: CTC grant and OJT proposal
sections.summary: The CTC grant's primary lever is project-based capital expenditure and lacks a six-month salary subsidy; the OJT proposal will be studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: While the CTC grant can support training fees and process redesign, its primary lever still remains project-based capital expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: It does not provide the aggressive six-month salary subsidy required to derisk the transition for an employer when a worker's productivity temporarily drops because of intensive AI training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: And many SMEs currently lack the internal capacity to design effective structured OJT, so my proposal provides the necessary, what we call, "design brains" through a dedicated pool of expert OJT consultants to ensure that the mastery that they achieve is both practical and is not just administrative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: I note the intent of the OJT and agree with the objectives behind the proposal, and it will be studied, considered in our NTUC's work, even as we chart possibilities in career counselling for the youths, and do possible pathways to innovate with the IHLs in career guidance and matches into internship and other possibilities.
